messages:
maya: Heads up — we need a short customer-facing update for ~20 trial + renewal accounts experiencing degraded answer relevance on private on‑prem model variant v2-quant since 2026-03-10. Monitoring flagged quality drift; customers started reporting increased hallucinations.

jonah: I can confirm. Our perf/infra telemetry shows a quantized-loader edge case: certain sequence-length paddings cause stale KV cache lookups. Root cause appears to be a regression introduced in the v2-quant packaging step.

maya: Ok. We should communicate: what happened, who is affected, immediate mitigation, ETA for fix, and a goodwill credit for impacted renewals. Keep it concise and prescriptive (customers hate long essays).

priyanka: Also include a short section for private/on‑prem ops: exact rollback command and where to send logs. Many of these are high-touch renewals — they want actionable steps.

jonah: Rollback plan: pin private clusters to v2-quant-rollback (build that matches last known-good kernel) and restart model workers. Command for customers with redwoodctl: 
```
redwoodctl model pin --model v2-quant-rollback
redwoodctl restart-model --model v2-quant-rollback --grace 30s
```
Log path: /var/log/redwood/model-loader.log. Expect each node restart to take ~45–90s; full throughput recovery 10–25 minutes depending on cluster size.

maya: Perfect. Draft for customers below — short, no engineering jargon. PTAL:

```
Hello — we’re writing about a temporary drop in answer relevance observed for the v2-quant model on private deployments. We identified a packaging regression that affected a subset of sequence-lengths, causing stale cache lookups.

What we’re doing: we’re rolling back the model to a verified build (v2-quant-rollback) and restarting model workers on affected clusters. If you self-manage, you can run the commands below; otherwise we will coordinate the rollback for you.

What you can do: run:
redwoodctl model pin --model v2-quant-rollback
redwoodctl restart-model --model v2-quant-rollback --grace 30s
Send us model-loader logs at /var/log/redwood/model-loader.log if the restart fails.

ETA: We expect resolution for most clusters within 2 hours of the rollback start.

Compensation: For impacted renewal customers we’re offering a one-time service credit to offset disruption; our CS rep will follow up with details.

If you’d like a live session to walk through verification or to run the rollback together, we’re scheduling office hours today at 10:30 PT.

Thanks for your patience — Maya, Customer Success
```

derek: Legal ok on credit wording as "one-time service credit"; avoid promising refunds or specific dollar amounts in the initial note.

linda: Sales/AMs — please prepare a short customer-specific follow-up for the renewal cohort (impact summary + how we’ll apply credit). I’ll assemble a list of affected customers and their renewal dates.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-138 | severity: P2 | owner: eng-runtime

jonah: Starting the rollback now on the first batch of dedicated clusters (4 nodes). I’ll update when the first cluster is healthy.

maya: Thanks. I’ll hold on sending the customer email until we have a confirm from Jonah that the first clusters recovered, then send an initial status update + office hours invite. :thumbsup:

jonah: Update: first cluster healthy at +12m, relevance scores back to baseline. Continuing rollout to remaining clusters.

maya: Fantastic. Sending update at 10:30 PT. I'll include the pinned commands and schedule link. If eng sees any deviation, ping this thread immediately.

priyanka: Noted — I’ll stand by to triage any private deployment help requests.

maya: Closing ask: eng confirm when rollout complete, legal & sales confirm customer wording + targeted credit list, CS to send the update.

jonah: Will confirm completion in this thread when done.
